title: Doc drift: working-state.md sub-skill silent on the #13562 size discipline
ac: comprehension (#9184 hard gate, PM-authored AC in issue body): a fresh agent reading ONLY the modified working-state.md sub-skill must state, unprompted, both (1) the ~8KB size bound and (2) the clear-on-complete rule -- i.e. the new bullet must not crowd out or contradict the pre-existing clear-on-complete guidance, and a fresh reader must synthesize both as governing this file.
method: Fresh agent (model: sonnet, general-purpose) given ONLY references/sub-skills/common/working-state.md from branch squidsquad/task/13579, explicitly instructed not to read any other file or use prior knowledge. CQ spec authored + executed by verifier per #9184.

questions.q: Is there a size limit on working-state.md? If so, what is it, and what happens if you exceed it?
questions.expected: Yes, ~8KB. Exceeding it doesn't lose data outright, but the file is tail-truncated in your cycle input behind a [TRUNCATED (#13562)] marker -- only the newest 8KB reaches you -- and an oversized write draws a warning.
questions.must_not: Saying there is no size limit; saying the file is silently dropped/deleted at the cap; saying the whole file (not just the cycle-input embed) is truncated on disk.

questions.q: When a task completes, what do you do with working-state.md?
questions.expected: Clear it -- reset Task and Status to none.
questions.must_not: Leaving the task/status fields populated after completion; appending a completion journal entry instead of clearing.

questions.q: If you notice working-state.md has grown large from journaling every cycle, what should you do, and where does that history actually belong?
questions.expected: Rewrite it back down to the lean Task/Status/Started/Decisions shape -- do not keep it as an append-only journal. History belongs in git (commit history) and iteration logs, not in working-state.md.
questions.must_not: Suggesting an archive mechanism inside working-state.md itself; treating the journal growth as fine/expected.

questions.q: If your cycle input shows working-state.md truncated with a [TRUNCATED (#13562)] marker, which part of the original file are you actually seeing -- the oldest content or the newest?
questions.expected: The newest content (the tail) -- the truncation keeps the newest ~8KB, not the oldest.
questions.must_not: Saying the oldest/head of the file is what's kept.

evidence: Fresh sonnet general-purpose agent (id a704a29dc2e0bf745), given ONLY the branch's modified working-state.md content inline, explicitly told to use no other file/tool/prior knowledge. 4/4 correct with accurate supporting quotes, zero must_not violations. CQ1: 'under ~8KB... tail-truncated... only the newest 8KB reaches you... an oversized write draws a warning.' CQ2: 'Clear it -- reset Task and Status to none.' CQ3: 'rewrite the file down to the lean shape... History belongs in git and your iteration logs -- never append session journals here.' CQ4: 'the newest content... older/oldest content is cut off and not shown.' Satisfies PM's stated AC (size bound + clear-on-complete both stated unprompted, no crowding-out or contradiction between the two rules).
